headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy consumers, such as data centers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, industrial companies), utility companies
news_headline: Governor Signs Bills Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, ensuring residential customers do not unfairly bear these generation and distribution expenses. This move aims to prevent increased utility bills for working families by making large energy users pay their fair share.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates
news_headline: Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed Senate Bill 553, strengthening water-use reporting requirements for data centers. This legislation aims to provide the Commonwealth with better data on water supplied to these facilities, addressing concerns about their impact on strained water resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes regulations for the siting of data centers and imposes limits on noise pollution to address community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: New Virginia Law Governs Data Center Siting, Disclosures
news_summary: Virginia enacted a new law, effective July 1, 2026, that requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts and disclose utility infrastructure. While it mandates studies, the law does not explicitly set noise limits or water caps, leaving some specifics to local discretion.
